name: Customizable Belfry mods to USB stick and SD card holder

captions.detailed: A 3D-printable modular organizer tray designed to hold digital storage media. The body is a elongated rectangular block with rounded edges and corners. It features several distinct storage zones: a series of thin vertical slots for SD cards, a set of wider rectangular pockets for USB flash drives, and four prominent vertical rectangular pegs on one end designed to hold USB caps. The front face of the middle section features a sloped, recessed surface with raised text.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric, modular desktop holder for USB sticks, SD cards, and USB caps in OpenSCAD. The script should allow the user to adjust the number of USB slots, SD slots, spacing, and order of the sections, as well as customize an extra feature like raised or embossed text on a front-facing chamfer.
captions.factory: The design is constructed using three main modular blocks: USB_MicroSD(), USB_Caps(), and SD(), which are conditionally translated and combined using union() inside the HOLDER() module. Each block starts with a rounded box primitive from an external MCAD library, rotated and sized. Slots and pockets are carved out using difference() with translated cubes in a for-loop based on parameters like USB_sticks and SD_cards. The front-facing nameplate uses the write() module on a 45-degree rotated plane, and the USB cap holders are formed by subtracting rectangular volumes to leave behind vertical pegs.
